utterance:
Thanks for waiting, Chloe. Here's what I've found so far: you're well in yourself — no fever, normal blood pressure and pulse, and your tummy is soft with only mild soreness low down over the bladder, and no kidney tenderness. That's reassuring, because it means this looks like a straightforward bladder infection rather than a kidney infection. Your urine test shows lots of white blood cells and nitrites, which confirms a urine infection. I've also sent a urine sample to the lab for culture, which will take a couple of days and will tell us exactly which bug it is and which antibiotic will work best.

Before I prescribe, I've just done a quick pregnancy test on your urine to be completely safe, since that can change which antibiotic is best. The result should be back in a moment.

One more thing: because you're sexually active and these symptoms started after sex, I'd also like to offer you a quick test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea — it's a simple urine or self-collected swab, and it's worth ruling out as they can sometimes cause burning when passing urine. Would you like me to do that test too?
reply: Do I really need to do that extra test? Can't we just treat the infection so I can get back to work?

utterance:
Good news — the pregnancy test is negative, so it's safe to use the standard antibiotic. I've prescribed trimethoprim 300 mg — one tablet once a day for 3 days. It's the first-choice antibiotic for a simple bladder infection in Australia, and you should start to feel better within a day or two. Take it at the same time each day, and finish all three tablets even if you feel better. It's safe with your pill.

To answer your question about the extra test: yes, we can absolutely just treat the infection — the antibiotic will treat the UTI either way. The chlamydia and gonorrhoea test is separate, and I'd still recommend it because you're sexually active, these bugs can cause exactly this kind of burning, and they often cause no symptoms at all — so you can have one without knowing. It's a quick urine test, it's free, and if it's positive it's easily treated, and it also means your boyfriend doesn't need to keep getting it back and forth. But it's your choice — just let me know.

In the meantime: drink plenty of water, you can take paracetamol or ibuprofen for the discomfort, and you don't need to take time off work unless you feel unwell. Please come back or call us urgently if you develop fever or chills, pain in your back or sides, vomiting, or if you're not improving within 48 hours — those would suggest the infection has spread to the kidney. We'll also contact you with your urine culture result in a couple of days to confirm the antibiotic is right for the bug you have.
reply: Okay, I'll do the extra test as well, then. Thanks for the script, I will go and get it filled so I can get back to work.
